12.11.text:
```cpp
process(shared_ptr<int>(p.get()));
```

p would be a dangling pointer after process is finished, because the copy we passed to process was independent of p, and as such, it also had a reference counter of 1. When it went out of scope its object--also was pointed to by p--was deleted.

12.31.name: 12.31.md
12.31.text: Unlike with a set, using a vector would log the line number a word appears on more than once. For example, if a word appears on a line multiple times, the vector would have duplicate line numbers. This is advantageous when we would like to know the occurrence of a word within a text. We could simply retrieve the size of the vector, which would be inaccurate in the case of a set. A vector has at least two disadvantage: 1) when we need to print the data, we would get duplicate lines; 2) the line numbers are not sorted and to sort them is slower than a set.
